page.overview:
What is fell beast?

Fell beasts and fell creatures were vague terms used to describe different monstrous, evil, and dangerous animals and other creatures that existed in Middle-earth (but not in Aman) from the Elder Days until the late Third Age. The Black Wings of the Nazgûl, in addition to Werewolves, were described as fell beasts. The Nazgûl themselves and hill-trolls are sometimes called fell creatures. In some cases Orcs, Trolls, and Dragons were distinguished from fell beasts.

When the Spring of Arda was marred, some beasts became monstrous creatures with horns and tusks. In Utumno, Melkor bred monsters of different shapes and kinds. At these times, Oromë came to Middle-earth as a hunter of monsters and fell creatures.

While Melkor was captured by the Valar, not all of his evil creatures were destroyed. They multiplied in the darkness, and even before the return of Morgoth, fell beasts of the North were roaming far and wide in the lands east of the Blue Mountains, so Nandor who inhabited woods of Eriador were frightened and fled from the plains to the hills or migrated to Ossiriand. Soon fell creatures came even to Beleriand over passes in the mountains and from the dark forests of the south. while the wilderness of Nan Dungortheb was inhabited by fell creatures of Ungoliant including spiders and other monsters.

Fell beasts continued to trouble Middle-earth during the Second Age and the Third Age. The Dúnedain of Gondor also faced threats from monsters in addition to Orcs and evil Men.
